findings.title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`) instead of checking for key presence or `is not None`. Because `0` is a valid integer value for both `age` (a report generated 0ms ago) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a payload containing `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1640995200000}` (or vice versa) will bypass the mutual-exclusion validation and be accepted with both fields present.

findings.title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` instead of matching by node id
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` whose keys and ordering are not guaranteed to align 1-to-1 with `error_ids` (for example, implementations that omit missing keys or return keys in arbitrary order). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can therefore associate an `event_id` with the wrong event payload or silently drop tail items. Look up each `node_id` in `events` (e.g. `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`).

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `if (!searchQuery.trim()) { return sorted; }` returns the unfiltered attribute list before the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check on line 67 runs. As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are displayed whenever the search box is empty and only hidden once the user types a search query.
